overview:
Norma Torres enters the general election as a heavy favorite in this Democratic-leaning district. She carries the advantages of incumbency in a seat that leans Democratic by six points, and her campaign has raised roughly $885,000 with $364,000 still on hand. Republican Mike Cargile has raised under $10,000 and reports just $448 in cash, leaving him little capacity to introduce himself to voters or counter any messaging. No outside groups have invested meaningfully on either side.

Prediction markets give Torres about a 96 percent chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings treat the seat as competitive. The expected margin sits near nineteen points, reflecting the district's lean, the incumbent's financial edge, and the absence of any credible challenge infrastructure. Barring an unforeseen shock, Torres is positioned for a comfortable re-election.
